title: Retention economy: when memory earns its keep
summary: A small pass that follows JelloBrain's interference problem into a bounded research note, then into 368's stronger fast-forgetting baseline and explicit retain/retrieve/investigate split. ThinkingJello is kept as a separate practical continuation: it carries prediction-error and visible-intervention lessons forward without claiming to solve JelloBrain's structural reversal failure.

nodes.claim: Research note asking whether conflicting experience should revise, retrieve, investigate or justify a new specialization, built from JelloBrain's cross-write interference and explicit causal-timing controls.
nodes.survived: The paper turns an intuitive growth story into bounded diagnostics: it reproduces the JelloBrain cross-write effect, shows why outcome-leaking selection is invalid, and records noise and coordinate controls that prevent gradient conflict from being treated as direct evidence for structural growth.
nodes.killed: Opposing updates do not prove that growth is necessary; gradient cosine is coordinate-dependent; unpredictable noise can create apparent conflict; and the proposed prospective growth protocol is specified future work rather than an executed result.

nodes.claim: Attacks the question 'when should a learner split?' with a strong fast-forgetting baseline, matched-cost active probes, and a hybrid that separates adaptation from retained memory and causal retrieval.
nodes.survived: Fast forgetting is the strong default; retained specialization can still help when old conditions recur; disagreement probes at adaptive times improve retrieval at matched observation cost; and storage itself does nothing unless retained models are actually reused.
nodes.killed: Prediction failure alone is not evidence for growth, the original prospective grower loses badly to fast forgetting on overall switching error, and in a no recurrence A→B→C world the system still stores memories without gaining prediction value—so successful admission cannot justify indefinite retention.

nodes.claim: A visible predictive organism demo with an internal copy, learned echo model and residual-driven interaction, carrying selected JelloBrain and GelatinIsland lessons into an inspectable browser system.
nodes.survived: In the simulated pond, the learned model explains 99.995–99.999% of future returns across six reported seeds when the body is stationary and learning is frozen; removing the internal copy drops that score to zero. The UI makes prediction, actual return, residual, intervention and saved adaptive state directly inspectable.
nodes.killed: The three frequency channels are engineered rather than emergent, the learned object is an impulse response rather than a grown JelloBrain material sheet, the JelloBrain reversal failure remains unresolved, and real-room microphone behavior is explicitly unvalidated.

edges.why: Paper explicitly says the manuscript develops its structural-specialization question from the JelloBrain experiments and includes a fresh reproduction of the upstream JelloBrain cross-write diagnostic.
368 opens by explicitly stating that it follows the research note When Should a Learner Split? in Paper, then attacks the note with a missing fast-forgetting baseline and new gates.
ThinkingJello's 'What carries forward' section explicitly names JelloBrain's separation of expected activity, meaningful mismatch and plasticity, while preserving its reversal failure as unresolved.
ThinkingJello explicitly names GelatinIsland as an upstream source for visible state, direct intervention and preservation of the whole adaptive organism rather than only a screenshot.

motifs.title: Storage is not retrieval
motifs.description: JelloBrain shows that structural writing can stabilize useful routes but can also interfere; Paper asks when another specialization is justified; 368 shows that cached models have no predictive value unless they are causally retrieved and that memories should eventually be priced by reuse.

motifs.title: Adapt, retain, retrieve and investigate are separate decisions
motifs.description: The line moves away from treating every surprise as a growth signal. A fast current model handles now; retention preserves a candidate; retrieval reuses old structure; active probing buys extra evidence only when ambiguity makes it worthwhile.

motifs.title: Prediction residual is useful only when its causal source is controlled
motifs.description: JelloBrain uses context-keyed negative-image cancellation to reveal hidden alternatives; ThinkingJello exposes a simpler outgoing-command/return prediction loop; SighImageSuper and IttnasNoruen independently warn that correlation with an action or discrepancy alone does not identify cause.
